note.note:
Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure:
  • Progressive reduction in hearing on the left side for ~3 weeks.  
  • Concurrent left-sided facial numbness around the ear and jawline.  
  • No specific precipitating event identified.

- Symptom timeline and progression:
  • Symptoms started “a few weeks” ago and persist daily.  
  • Intermittent tinnitus (“ringing”) in the same ear; dizziness sometimes accompanies tinnitus.  
  • Impacting ability to train/work as a professional jockey.

- ENT symptoms:
  • Throat swelling/closure sensation: Denied.  
  • Voice change: Denied.  
  • Dysphagia/odynophagia: Denied.  
  • Drooling: Not reported.  
  • Nasal/ocular symptoms: Chronic nasal polyps (spray used PRN); no acute nasal congestion or ocular symptoms.  
  • Stridor/noisy breathing, dyspnea: Denied.  
  • Distribution of swelling: None; reports only numbness.  
  • Ear symptoms: Left-sided hearing loss, intermittent tinnitus; denies ear pain, discharge, pruritus.  
  • Neck symptoms: None.

- Relevant past episodes and treatments:
  • Past diagnosis of nasal polyps; uses intranasal spray as needed (name/dose/route/frequency not documented).  
  • Remote history of “labyrinthitis” (details not provided).  
  • No previous similar facial numbness or hearing loss reported.  
  • No prior ED visits, hospitalizations, or injection therapy for ENT issues.

- Allergies and current medications:
  • Latex – allergic.  
  • Medications:  
    – Intranasal spray for nasal polyps (name and dose/route/frequency not documented).  
    – Rennie (OTC antacid, dose/frequency not documented).  
  • No other regular or rescue medications; no epinephrine auto-injector.

- Social context:
  • Occupation: Professional jockey; lives with partner (patient initially stated living alone, later clarified living with partner – conflict noted).

Objective:
- Observable swelling: None reported/visualized during video consult.  
- Airway/breathing: No respiratory distress; patient speaking in full sentences.  
- Mental status: Alert, oriented; expresses anxiety about seriousness of condition.  
- Vitals and physical examination: Not recorded (video consultation only).  
- Additional observers: None present on call.

Assessment:
- Unilateral (left) sensorineural or conductive hearing loss with ipsilateral facial numbness and intermittent tinnitus; possible Bell’s palsy considered by clinician.  
  • Justification: Unilateral facial sensory change and otologic symptoms without systemic features; requires cranial nerve and otoscopic examination to confirm.  
- No current features of airway compromise or acute otologic infection.  
- Anxiety regarding potential serious diagnosis.

Plan:
- Same-day face-to-face clinic appointment arranged for full neurological and otoscopic examination.  
  • Admin team to book patient into central London clinic; patient instructed to phone support team after 5 minutes to confirm slot.  
- Diagnostic focus: Cranial nerve exam, otoscopy, audiometry as indicated to evaluate for Bell’s palsy or other neurological/otologic pathology.  
- Reassurance provided that condition is unlikely to be life-threatening; definitive assessment still required today.  
- Red-flag advice: Seek urgent care (call emergency services) if sudden worsening of hearing, new facial weakness, difficulty speaking/swallowing, vision changes, severe dizziness, or any breathing difficulty.  
- Medication/management adjustments: None initiated pending in-person review.  
- Follow-up: Further management plan (e.g., corticosteroids, antiviral therapy, ENT referral, imaging) to be determined after physical examination.  
- Documentation: Support team contact number placed in notes for patient access.

Quality checks (document_quality):
● Missing but clinically expected elements:
  – Objective physical findings (cranial nerve exam, facial movement assessment, otoscopy, audiometry, vitals).  
  – Detailed medication list (exact nasal spray, dosing).  
  – Formal allergy list beyond latex.  
  – History of varicella or vaccination status (re: Ramsay Hunt differential) and availability of prior imaging.

● Internal conflicts:
  – Patient first reported living alone, later stated living with partner (conflict noted).

● Transcript quality:
  – Generally clear; occasional minor inaudible segments but no loss of key clinical data.
